subject: Uptime baseline adjustment + burst-window credit proposal (CloudSynergy)
messages:
From: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@cloudsynergy.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: opslead@cloudsynergy.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Uptime baseline - seeking a carveout for daily burst windows

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's routing options. Before we move to legal, we need to confirm how the uptime baseline and monthly credit calculations would work for our workload. A couple of realities on our side:

- We have daily peak windows (US-east mornings) that can increase request volume by ~6x for 45–90 minutes; these are unpredictable but consistent.
- For business continuity we need an uptick tolerance during those bursts without triggering disproportionate monthly credits.

Can Redwood propose a template carveout or an alternative credit ladder that:
1) preserves the standard 99.9% monthly baseline for steady-state traffic,
2) applies a temporary ‘burst window’ tolerance that reduces credit exposure for short, high-intensity episodes, and
3) includes a clear measurement method (how you compute downtime during a rapid burst).

I've attached a short traffic export (CloudSynergy_traffic_report_Q3.csv) to illustrate the pattern. Ideally we want a simple, deterministic credit table that legal can accept without multiple redlines.

Would appreciate a suggested wording we can slot into the SOW.

Best,
Sarah Ng
Head of Platform Reliability
CloudSynergy

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@cloudsynergy.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime baseline - seeking a carveout for daily burst windows

Sarah — thanks for the data dump, that was helpful. Looping in Laura (Enterprise) and Ben (Pricing) for the contract framing.

High level proposal from Redwood to address the three asks:

- Baseline: keep monthly uptime baseline at 99.9% for all traffic (steady-state).
- Burst-window tolerance: define up to two recurring daily windows (Client-configurable) where short-duration service degradation up to X% of window time does not escalate to full-month credits. Example: 45–120 minute windows, tolerated degradation up to 6 minutes per window before crediting begins.
- Measurement: use rolling 1-minute sampling aggregated to monthly: credits trigger only for minutes outside of configured burst windows; minutes within an approved burst window are measured but only counted for credit if continuous degradation exceeds the tolerated minutes threshold.

We believe this preserves standard availability guarantees while protecting you from outsized credit exposure during short, high-intensity spikes. Ben — I've attached an initial credit ladder workbook (Redwood_credit_table_v1.xlsx) with illustrative numbers (three tiers). Please review and propose exact credit percentages for the tolerated ranges.

Request: Sarah, can you confirm typical daily window start/end times (local to US-east) and whether you need more than two recurring windows? Also confirm whether your legal team prefers explicit minute-based language or percentage-based language in the SOW.

Next steps: if you confirm window times I can ask Legal to draft a short contract clause we can iterate on.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@cloudsynergy.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime baseline - seeking a carveout for daily burst windows

Sarah — quick follow from Pricing/legal POV.

- Configurable tolerated minutes: yes — we can make the tolerated minutes an account-level parameter documented in the SOW (example clause provided below). That lets you tune during pilot without re-contracting.

- Credit calculation: credits will be computed on total monthly impacted minutes but the ladder will only apply to minutes that exceeded tolerated minutes AND occurred outside the configured burst window exception. If a sustained outage during a burst window goes beyond the tolerated minutes threshold, we will count only the excess minutes toward credit calculation (not the entire burst window).

Proposed clause (copy/paste friendly):
"For recurring burst windows specified in Schedule A, Customer may designate up to two recurring daily windows. During each configured window Redwood will tolerate up to N minutes of service degradation per window without triggering monthly service credits. Service credits, if any, will be calculated on the minutes in excess of the tolerated minutes per window aggregated across the month per the credit ladder in Schedule B."

Ben — suggested values we initially recommend for pilot: tolerated minutes = 6 per window; credit ladder: 99.9–99.5% = 10% monthly credit; 99.4–98.5% = 25%; <98.5% = 50%. (We can lower the credit percentages for enterprise commitments.)

If that sound acceptable I can have Legal draft the SOW language and include the configurable field in the console (so your SREs can change it).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Pricing & Contracts
Redwood Inference
